Attat!

aha! (a sudden realisation)

(vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

Lewis & Short (s.v. atat, also spelt attat, attatae): joy, pain, wonder, fright, warning. Of a dismayed discovery it is “uh-oh” (see oh no!).

Other words

  • Hahahae! — aha! ha!

    also used · classical · Plaut. Poen. 768: Hahahae, jam teneō quid sit, perspexī modo.

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut.)

    Lewis & Short (s.v. ha): laughter or derision; here the laugh of a man who has seen through something.

  • Ehem! — ah! I see

    also used · classical · Plaut. Mil. 36b: Ehem, sciō jam quid vīs dīcere.

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

Examples

  • attat! hoc illud est: hinc illae lacrumae

    Aha! so that’s it: hence those tearsTer. And. 125–126

  • attat, sciō cūr tē patrem adsimulēs esse et mē fīlium

    aha, I know why you pretend to be my father and me your sonPlaut. Capt. 1007

  • Hahahae, jam teneō quid sit, perspexī modo.

    Aha, now I get it; I’ve just seen through it.Plaut. Poen. 768

  • Ehem, sciō jam quid vīs dīcere.

    Ah, now I know what you mean.Plaut. Mil. 36b

  • Attat, quem quaerēbam!

    Aha, the very person I was looking for!Traupman 102

See also I get it!, oh no!, oh!.
